diagnosis: Resident /wc launch envelopes that carried RESIDENTE_POOL but omitted an explicit POOL <id> were classified UNBATCHED. That silently disabled deterministic pooled sharding and POOL_TAIL_RESCUE, concentrating concurrent workers on the same leading claims and increasing bounded CREATE_EXISTS/no-allocation outcomes. The canonical mission prompt already names POOL PROD-01, so the defect was a compatibility/parser gap rather than a missing allocator or scheduler.
intervention: Made WORKER_FRESH_LAUNCH_POLICY_V1 the singular launch-envelope parser owner. On /wc only, RESIDENTE_POOL with no explicit RUN/BATCH/POOL identity now aliases to the existing CURRENT rolling pool PROD-01 (launch_class=POOL, batch_id=POOL-PROD-01, pool_id=PROD-01). Explicit RUN/BATCH/POOL identities retain precedence. Downstream BATCH/POOL predicates must consume parsed launch_class/beacon identity rather than re-parse literal tokens, so existing sharding/residency/POOL_TAIL_RESCUE apply without any new scheduler, queue, CURRENT, planner, provider or family. Stable /w remains explicit-only. Added a regression guard tying the alias to CURRENT mission pool identity and preserving canonical prompt aliases.
